problem_motivation.content: Sustainable deployment is urgently needed as PV scales to multi-terawatt levels.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: As photovoltaics (PVs) scale from one to multiple terawatts over the next decade, ensuring sustainable deployment is urgently required.

problem_motivation.content: c-Si PVs will create major waste and face difficult recycling challenges.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: Crystalline silicon (c-Si) PVs, the current industry standard, will generate an estimated 160 million tonnes of waste by 2050, and there remains complex technoeconomic challenges associated with their recycling.

problem_motivation.content: Critical circularity challenges must be addressed for perovskite PV market entry.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: At this pivotal juncture when perovskite PVs begin to enter the market, this review examines the critical circularity challenges that must be addressed: substitution of scarce raw materials, scalable recycling protocols, cost-effective stack delamination, safe lead sequestration, and policy frameworks to encourage circularity across the device lifecycle with effective incentives.

problem_motivation.content: Rapid PV growth creates urgent sustainability challenges in waste management and material circularity.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: But with this rapid growth, there are urgent sustainability challenges, particularly regarding the management of PV waste and the circularity of materials used in solar modules

problem_motivation.content: Resource depletion, production impacts, and end-of-life management remain unresolved at multi-terawatt scale.

problem_motivation.evidence_span: policy frameworks developed for legacy PV technologies must adapt to the distinct material flows and risks of MHP tandems, incentivizing eco-design and full material traceability.

causal_claim.content: Panel complexity leads to disposal or low-value repurposing that limits circularity and poses environmental problems.
causal_claim.evidence_span: As a result, many panels in the USA are disposed of via landfill, while in Europe they are often repurposed, for instance, as building aggregates in roads, in ways that limit true materials circularity and continue to pose environmental challenges

causal_claim.content: Glass contamination causes downgraded reuse rather than closed-loop recycling.
causal_claim.evidence_span: due to contamination, this glass is typically downgraded to cement or aggregates with reduced environmental benefits compared to recycling glass back to sheet

causal_claim.content: Tandem devices can exceed single-junction c-Si efficiency limits by combining complementary absorbers.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Multi-junction devices combine sub-cells absorbing in complementary parts of the solar spectrum, raising theoretical efficiency limits well beyond the practical limit of single-junction c-Si PVs

causal_claim.content: Higher efficiency yields more energy per area and lowers environmental impact per kWh.
causal_claim.evidence_span: These efficiency gains translate into higher energy yield per unit area, which therefore lowers the environmental impact per kWh generated.

causal_claim.content: Replacing c-Si with thin-film absorbers could avoid c-Si-related carbon, energy, and recycling burdens.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Replacing the c-Si cell can allow MHP-based tandems to overcome the challenges inherent to c-Si modules, such as its high carbon dioxide equivalent (CO2eq) footprint, high energy cost of production, and challenging and costly recycling.

causal_claim.content: Lower material use and low-temperature processing reduce manufacturing carbon footprint.
causal_claim.evidence_span: perovskite cells require lower material use than c-Si cells, and can be processed via low-temperature methods that enable reduced CO2eq footprints during manufacture

causal_claim.content: Soluble functional layers open simpler and cheaper recycling routes.
causal_claim.evidence_span: the functional layers in MHP cells are largely soluble in relatively mild solvents, which opens up recycling routes for the MHP cell(s)23,24 that are potentially simpler and more cost-effective than c-Si recycling

causal_claim.content: Early failure of the MHP sub-cell could erase tandem sustainability gains and worsen c-Si waste growth.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Premature EOL of the MHP sub-cell could negate the overall sustainability benefits gained from the transition to tandems with MHPs, and have the potential to exacerbate exponential c-Si waste volumes expected during this period, unless effective methods for recycling the c-Si bottom cell are developed.

causal_claim.content: Switching to tandem modules can prematurely decommission working c-Si systems and increase waste.
causal_claim.evidence_span: an unintended consequence of transitioning from single-junction c-Si PV to MHP-based tandems is that older, working c-Si systems are prematurely decommissioned and replaced with newer tandem modules, further accelerating waste volumes unless viable c-Si reuse markets can be established

causal_claim.content: Without policy intervention, tandem adoption is likely to shorten existing PV lifetimes in some countries.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Without policy intervention, MHP-based tandems are likely to shorten the lifetime of current single junction PV in countries with strong incentives for low carbon electricity generation and lower carbon emissions

causal_claim.content: Transporting bulky panels to centralized recycling adds hidden carbon cost.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The transportation of bulky, heavy c-Si and MHP tandem panels to the centralized PV recycling infrastructure also adds a hidden CO2eq cost to the total emissions

causal_claim.content: Perovskite versatility enables integration with many tandem configurations.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Their versatility supports their integration into diverse tandem configurations, including with c-Si67, copper indium gallium diselenide (CIGSe)68, kesterites69, cadmium telluride (CdTe)70, organic PV71, and all-perovskite combinations22

causal_claim.content: Combining tandem efficiency with thin-film low-temperature processing creates sustainability opportunities.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Such MHP-based tandem technologies combine the high efficiency potential of tandem architectures with the low-temperature processing and thin-film material use characteristic of perovskite absorbers, creating opportunities to meet performance requirements while delivering sustainability improvements.

causal_claim.content: Optimized MHP/Si systems can yield up to 30% more annual energy than single-junction c-Si.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Optimized MHP/Si PV systems can achieve annual energy yields (electrical energy produced by PVs, in kWh, in real-world scenarios)81 up to 30% higher than single-junction c-Si PVs under real-world conditions82.

causal_claim.content: Lower perovskite temperature coefficient gives a relative advantage in warm conditions.
causal_claim.evidence_span: perovskites exhibit a lower temperature coefficient (typically –0.15% to –0.3% °C–1  vs. silicon's –0.4% to –0.5% °C–1), providing a relative advantage for perovskite-based devices in warmer conditions

causal_claim.content: Bandgap and thickness tailoring to location can maximize output and improve material utilization.
causal_claim.evidence_span: By tailoring the design of perovskite solar cells, primarily through bandgap tuning (e.g., via compositional changes) and absorber layer thickness optimization87, to specific locations and operating conditions, it is possible to maximize their energy output and achieve improved material utilization ratios

causal_claim.content: Thin-film, low-weight tandems ease building integration and reduce installation cost.
causal_claim.evidence_span: all-thin film tandems thus enable low-weight, high-specific-power modules manufactured via low-temperature processes that facilitate easier integration into existing building structures and reduce installation costs

causal_claim.content: Higher energy yield reduces balance-of-system needs, land use, and lifecycle emissions per power generated.
causal_claim.evidence_span: the higher energy yield in MHP-based tandem PVs translates directly into sustainability benefits by delivering more electricity per manufacturing energy and material input than conventional c-Si PVs, thereby reducing balance-of-system requirements, land use, and lifecycle greenhouse gas emissions per unit power generated

causal_claim.content: Low-temperature processability can shorten energy payback time and lower embodied energy.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Owing to the low temperature processability of the MHP top-cell, perovskite-silicon tandems can achieve shorter energy payback times and lower embodied energy than single-junction c-Si PVs

causal_claim.content: Extending service life from 10 to 25 years halves GWP without changing EPBT.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Extending service life from 10 to 25 years halves GWP while unalters EPBT88,101.

causal_claim.content: 4-T tandems are easier to recycle because independently fabricated sub-cells can be separated at end of life.
causal_claim.evidence_span: 4-T tandems offer recycling advantage because each sub-cell is fabricated independently and mechanically stacked, allowing for easy separation at EOL of either sub-cell.

causal_claim.content: Monolithic integration makes recovery from 2-T tandems much more difficult.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Recovering various highly valuable materials from 2-T tandem solar cells is significantly more complicated due to the monolithic integration of the sub-cells.

causal_claim.content: Water-based recovery significantly reduces resource depletion and lowers LCOE.
causal_claim.evidence_span: which significantly reduce overall resource depletion and lower the LCOE

causal_claim.content: Indium scarcity and thick ITO requirements drive supply instability, price volatility, and high material demand.
causal_claim.evidence_span: This results in supply instability and price volatility, with costs reaching ~$452/kg122. The high DPRs arise from the scarcity of In, and the relatively thick ITO layers required to have low sheet resistance, which elevates material demands.

causal_claim.content: 4-T modules require far more TCO material than 2-T architectures.
causal_claim.evidence_span: A 4-T module requires three or four thick transparent electrode layers (Box 2), increasing the total TCO material requirement to roughly five times that of a 2-T architecture.

causal_claim.content: Using a 10 nm IZO-based interconnection layer in a 35%-efficient tandem can lower indium DPR to about 23%.
causal_claim.evidence_span: A 35%-efficient tandem device with a 10 nm-thick IZO-based ICL can reduce the DPR to about 23%67

causal_claim.content: Ultrathin Au interconnection layers substantially increase demand-to-production ratio and primary energy demand, making Au undesirable.
causal_claim.evidence_span: An extremely thin Au ICL of 0.4 nm results in a DPR of approximately 1.4% and contributes up to 42% of the total primary energy demand in MHP/MHP tandem devices, making gold an unfavourable option from environmental and economical perspectives.

causal_claim.content: Cross-linking mixed functional molecules into co-SAM networks improves stability.
causal_claim.evidence_span: cross-linking mixed functional molecules to form covalently interconnected interfacial networks (i.e., co-SAMs143,144) can lead to improved stability

causal_claim.content: SAMs are considered more sustainable because they use far less material than polymeric HTLs.
causal_claim.evidence_span: they are widely considered more sustainable than using organic charge transport layers because they use orders of magnitude less material, i.e., sub-nanometre SAMs versus conventional >10-nm-thick polymeric PTAA or doped Spiro-OMeTAD HTLs.

causal_claim.content: Spontaneous SAM monolayer formation removes the need for hygroscopic dopants and reduces compositional variability.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Because SAMs spontaneously form ordered monolayers upon solution deposition, they eliminate the need for hygroscopic dopants required in organic HTLs, thereby reducing compositional variability.

causal_claim.content: Halogen-functionalized SAMs improve textured-interface performance by enabling coverage, hole extraction, and defect passivation.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Using conjugated halogen-functionalized SAMs can achieve uniform coverage on rough pyramidal surfaces, achieving improved hole extraction and effective defect passivation on textured interfaces145.

causal_claim.content: Low operating current in tandems reduces resistive losses and permits higher-resistance, silver-lean metallization schemes.
causal_claim.evidence_span: tandem cells possess a lower operating current that significantly reduces resistive power losses, making them more tolerant of higher-resistance grids, and encouraging silver-lean PV technologies

causal_claim.content: High deposition temperatures degrade perovskite absorbers and compromise amorphous-silicon passivation in tandems.
causal_claim.evidence_span: the high deposition temperatures can degrade the perovskite absorber and compromise the amorphous silicon passivation layers of the cells.

causal_claim.content: Hybrid electrodes may aid tandem integration by allowing lower-temperature, solution-processed fabrication.
causal_claim.evidence_span: These hybrid electrodes may facilitate tandem integration by enabling lower-temperature and solution-processed electrode fabrication.

causal_claim.content: The efficiency penalty of indium-free tandems is increasingly offset by much lower material criticality.
causal_claim.evidence_span: the ~10% relative efficiency trade-off is increasingly offset by a 90% reduction in material criticality.

causal_claim.content: Photonic curing enables scalable low-energy processing on heat-sensitive substrates.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Photonic curing, which uses millisecond light pulses for rapid, low-energy processing, enables scalable, roll-to-roll fabrication on heat-sensitive substrates.

causal_claim.content: Work-function engineering via doping or buffer layers improves efficiency and long-term stability.
causal_claim.evidence_span: work function engineering through doping or interfacial buffer layers improves device efficiency and long-term stability.

causal_claim.content: Because perovskites are water-soluble, Pb2+ can be released during deployment through water exposure or fire.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Given the water solubility of MHPs, Pb2+ can readily be released to the environment upon real-world deployment through contact with water, or released in the vapour phase during a fire.

causal_claim.content: Applying phosphate-buffered functionalized polymer film reduced Pb leaching into water to below the US drinking-water limit.
causal_claim.evidence_span: By applying the PFPF, the content of Pb2+ leached into water decreased from 12.39 mg L-1 to 10.1 mg L-1, within the US requirements of <15 mg L-1 for safe drinking water210.

causal_claim.content: Hydroxyl- and carboxyl-rich supramolecular complexes enabled Pb sequestration and sharply reduced Pb leaching.
causal_claim.evidence_span: the high density of hydroxyl and carboxyl groups in the supramolecular complex enabled Pb2+ sequestration214, decreasing the Pb leaching rate in flowing water by a factor of 18.

causal_claim.content: Recycling challenges known from c-Si are expected to be amplified in MHP/Si devices.
causal_claim.evidence_span: the engineering issues that currently trouble c-Si PV about differences in panel composition, low material value and difficulties in delamination will be amplified with MHP/Si devices

causal_claim.content: Lower silver content improves deployability but weakens recycling economics by reducing recoverable value.
causal_claim.evidence_span: with the reducing material content per Wp of high-cost material like silver

causal_claim.content: Mandatory EPDs would improve transparency and help buyers make informed environmental choices.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Mandatory EPDs would provide greater transparency for the MHP industry to help buyers make informed decisions about the products’ environmental credentials.

causal_claim.content: If enforced, mandatory EPDs would create a level playing field and incentivize sustainability-oriented innovation rather than efficiency-only competition.
causal_claim.evidence_span: If this approach were enforced, this would create a level playing field for all manufacturers to design for sustainability from the outset. Manufacturers would be incentivized to innovate perovskite technologies with decreasing impact on the environment, instead of the current status quo of competing on ever-increasing cell efficiency and energy yield.

causal_claim.content: Replacing Ag and Au grids with Cu-based or printed carbon contacts can significantly reduce environmental impact.
causal_claim.evidence_span: replacing Ag and Au grids with copper-based contacts or printed carbon electrodes can significantly reduce the environmental impact of the tandem PV module

causal_claim.content: Increased efficiency can drive repowering and early retirement of modules.
causal_claim.evidence_span: technological developments (such as increased efficiency) can lead to ‘repowering’ and early retirement of modules after less than 10 years operation.

causal_claim.content: Reducing Ag content supports terawatt-scale deployment but reduces recycling incentives because Ag is a main recoverable value stream.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Reducing the Ag content per panel is important for enabling TW-scale deployment, however, lower Ag content also reduces the economic incentives for recycling panels, as Ag is one of the main high-value materials recovered during PV recycling.

mechanism_principle.content: Complex panel construction makes recycling technically and economically difficult.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: The complex construction of c-Si panels, including durable encapsulants and multi-layered assemblies, presents substantial technical and economic barriers to effective recycling

mechanism_principle.content: Premature replacement is driven by better panel efficiency and lower PV cost relative to supporting infrastructure.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: This is driven by several factors, especially the increasing efficiency of new panels, and the reduced cost of PV compared with auxiliary infrastructure, such as frames, grid connection, and inverters

mechanism_principle.content: Keeping c-Si modules operating longer lowers total embodied carbon across primary and secondary supply chains.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: keeping c-Si modules operational for as long as possible reduces the overall embodied CO2eq footprint of the primary c-Si and secondary MHP supply chain

mechanism_principle.content: Environmental gains come from thin printable absorbers, low-temperature fabrication, and avoiding silicon purification.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: These improvements arise from thin printable absorbers, lower-temperature fabrication for the entire tandem device, and the elimination of energy-intensive silicon purification.

mechanism_principle.content: Low lead inventory plus encapsulation, sequestration, and recycling infrastructure make closed-loop recovery technically feasible.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: This low material inventory, combined with encapsulation, sequestration and existing industrial recycling infrastructures, makes closed-loop recovery technically feasible.

mechanism_principle.content: Silicon-free tandems have much lower cumulative energy demand mainly because silicon wafer refinement dominates Si-based tandem impacts.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: the cumulative energy demand of silicon-free perovskite tandems is nearly six times lower than that of Si-based tandems, a difference attributed almost entirely to the energy-intensive silicon wafer refinement cycle, which dominates the impact of the latter111

mechanism_principle.content: For Si-free tandems, key carbon impacts come from manufacturing energy, TCO deposition, and encapsulation.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: the main impacts stem from manufacturing energy (notably vacuum deposition steps), deposition of transparent conducting oxides, and encapsulation112–115

mechanism_principle.content: Stability improvement from co-SAMs is attributed to suppression of diffusion, delamination, and chemical degradation under stress.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: by suppressing molecular diffusion, interfacial delamination, and chemical degradation under heat and illumination

mechanism_principle.content: Lower mobility in SnO2-based TCOs requires higher carrier concentrations, which raise free-carrier absorption and reduce NIR transmission.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: SnO2-based TCOs generally exhibit lower intrinsic mobility, requiring higher carrier concentrations (≥1020-1021 cm-3)180,181 to achieve low resistivity, which enhances free-carrier absorption and shifts the plasma edge into the near-infrared, reducing NIR transmission relative to higher-mobility TCOs182.

mechanism_principle.content: Aliovalent doping in ZnO adds n-type carriers, and low effective electron mass supports higher mobility and conductivity at lower carrier density, improving NIR transparency.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Substitution of Zn2+ with Al3+ or Ga3+ introduces n-type carriers, while the low effective electron mass (0.24-0.3m0)186 in ZnO supports relatively high mobility and adequate conductivity at lower carrier concentrations, improving near-infrared transparency for optimized GZO films187.

hypothesis_statement.content: Integrating materials, technoeconomic, and policy perspectives can co-optimize performance and sustainability.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: By integrating the materials, technoeconomic and policy dimensions that go beyond conventional lifecycle assessments, we outline actionable strategies to co-optimize device performance and sustainability.

hypothesis_statement.content: MHP-based PV recycling could enable closed-loop recovery and lower environmental footprint.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: These recycling processes possible with MHP-based PVs could enable closed-loop material recovery and reduce the environmental footprint of solar energy systems

hypothesis_statement.content: ZnO-based TCOs are promising indium-free alternatives.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: Zinc oxide–based TCOs, particularly aluminium-doped zinc oxide (AZO) and gallium-doped zinc oxide (GZO), are promising In-free alternatives.

hypothesis_statement.content: Hybrid electrodes are a promising route to combine performance, stability, and sustainability.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: Another promising route to achieve high performance, stability and sustainability is to develop hybrid electrodes, such as AgNWs embedded within metal oxides or CPs161,197.

hypothesis_statement.content: Lead sequestration is presented as a key strategy for preventing Pb release after encapsulation failure.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: Pb sequestration is a key approach to doing this.

hypothesis_statement.content: The policy framework should reflect the global solar market and harmonize to stringent regulations.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: The policy framework should reflect the global nature of the solar market, whereby solar manufacturers operating worldwide standardize their products to meet the most stringent regulations, making them universally compliant227.

hypothesis_statement.content: Perovskite waste may need to be separated from c-Si waste streams, requiring dedicated infrastructure and finance mechanisms.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: it may be necessary for MHPs to be kept separate from traditional c-Si waste streams, due to the need to isolate the reusable elements from EOL for producing new panels, and this would require separate infrastructure, collection streams, and finance mechanisms

hypothesis_statement.content: The paper recommends mandatory environmental product declarations for MHP manufacturers.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: It is a recommendation of this paper that MHP manufacturers should provide mandatory Environmental Product Declarations (EPD).

hypothesis_statement.content: Sustainable terawatt-scale deployment requires coordinated advances in materials, manufacturing, durability, end-of-life management, and policy.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: sustainable TW-scale deployment requires coordinated advances across the materials used, manufacturing practices, improving the durability of the devices, and end-of-life management, together with an effective international policy framework for incentivizing circularity.

hypothesis_statement.content: Developing high-performance indium-free TCOs is a promising route to combine sustainability and efficiency.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: developing high-performance indium-free TCOs offers a path to combine sustainability with efficiency in tandem solar cells.

hypothesis_statement.content: The authors strongly recommend a systems approach to optimize environmental performance.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: we strongly recommend taking a systems approach to realize the optimal environmental performance of MHP-based tandems.

hypothesis_statement.content: Designing devices, standards, and takeback systems together could make commercial tandems green across their full lifecycle.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: Designing the devices, standards, and takeback systems together could make future commercial MHP-based tandems green not just in their electricity production, but across their entire lifecycle.

evidence_result.content: Lab-scale perovskite/Si tandems have surpassed 34% efficiency.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Laboratory-scale demonstration of perovskite/Si tandems with 1 cm2 device area have already surpassed 34% efficiency

evidence_result.content: Repowering with higher-efficiency panels often brings CO2 benefit only after 15 years, though financial benefit may appear after 8 years.
evidence_result.evidence_span: whilst in some scenarios a financial benefit is obtained by replacing c-Si single-junction modules after 8 years of service, a CO2eq emissions benefit (on replacement with higher-efficiency panels) is not typically realized until 15 years of service

evidence_result.content: First-mile transport contributes relatively little to lifecycle emissions but can be costly in remote areas.
evidence_result.evidence_span: While this CO2eq contribution is relatively small compared to total lifecycle emissions, ‘first-mile’ transport costs to central distribution centres can be high, particularly in remote regions.

evidence_result.content: Perovskite/Si tandems reached 34.85% and all-perovskite tandems reached 30.1% efficiency.
evidence_result.evidence_span: By mid-2025, perovskite/Si two-terminal tandem solar cells have achieved record efficiencies of 34.85% (modules up to 33%), surpassing the efficiency limits of single-junction c-Si PVs72. All-perovskite tandems have reached 30.1% power conversion efficiency (PCE)72

evidence_result.content: Median LCA values show MHP/Si tandems slightly outperform c-Si, while all-perovskite tandems perform substantially better.
evidence_result.evidence_span: the median primary energy demand for a laboratory-scale MHP/Si tandem module is 13 840 MJ kWp–1... this energy demand corresponds to a median energy-payback time (EPBT) of 1.3 years and global warming potential (GWP) of 915 gCO₂eq kWp-1. These are still marginally improved over c-Si single-junction PVs, which have typical values of 1.5 years and 1224 g CO2eq kWp-1, respectively. But switching to all-perovskite tandems substantially reduces both indicators, with median a EPBT of 0.33 years and GHG intensity of 209 gCO2eq kWp-1

evidence_result.content: Pilot lines and outdoor prototypes support the environmental and durability claims.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Industrial pilot lines are validating these environmental assessments, and outdoor prototypes already pass standard damp-heat and thermal-cycling industrial tests16.

evidence_result.content: Recovered c-Si cells yielded tandem efficiency close to fresh-cell tandems.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The tandems built on these recovered c-Si cells show a PCE of 25.7%, which is comparable to those fabricated from the fresh cells (26.3%)106.

evidence_result.content: Projected indium demand-production ratios are extremely high for TW-scale tandems.
evidence_result.evidence_span: the projected DPRs of In are on average 761% for perovskite-silicon and 440% for all-perovskite tandems

evidence_result.content: Indium in TCOs contributes 24–50% of total primary material energy demand in all-perovskite tandems.
evidence_result.evidence_span: the In content of the TCO also accounts for 24–50% of the total materials primary energy demand in MHP/MHP tandems

evidence_result.content: A conventional 20 nm ITO interconnection layer yields about 70% indium DPR in a 25.4% tandem.
evidence_result.evidence_span: A conventional 20-nm ITO ICL in a 25.4% tandem corresponds to an indium DPR of about 70%

evidence_result.content: In MHP/Si tandems, the c-Si wafer dominates embodied energy and replacing Si with a perovskite bottom cell cuts primary energy by over 99%.
evidence_result.evidence_span: our calculations show that the single-crystalline c-Si wafer accounts for ~95% of the total the embodied energy of the tandem (Figure 2c), consistent with prior LCAs (Box 3)88. Since MHP absorbers require orders of magnitude less energy to produce than c-Si, replacing Si with a perovskite bottom cell reduces primary energy consumption by >99%

evidence_result.content: AZO and GZO achieve moderate sheet resistance and high visible transmittance.
evidence_result.evidence_span: These materials can achieve sheet resistances of 29–62.5 Ω sq⁻¹ and visible transmittance of approximately 83-94%188–192.

evidence_result.content: Perovskite-silicon tandems with AZO TCEs have reached efficiencies above 28%, near ITO-based devices.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Perovskite-silicon tandem cells with AZO-based TCEs have demonstrated PCEs exceeding 28%, close to those achieved using ITO188.

evidence_result.content: At an optimal AgNW loading, silver demand corresponds to a low DPR, supporting feasibility as an indium-saving alternative.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The optimal AgNW density for replacing TCOs has been estimated to be approximately 120 mg m–2, balancing high optical transmittance with low sheet resistance198. Assuming a PCE of 25%, this Ag loading corresponds to a DPR of 2.1% ... rendering AgNW networks a highly feasible alternative to alleviate In usage.

evidence_result.content: Indium-free tandems are nearing 25% efficiency, though still below ITO/IZO record devices.
evidence_result.evidence_span: perovskite/silicon tandems utilizing ALD-deposited AZO as an interconnection layer have recently demonstrated sub-cell efficiencies of 24.94%199. While this remains below the record 35.0% achieved with optimized ITO/IZO stacks200

evidence_result.content: A hole transport layer based on alkoxy-poly tetra ethylene glycol captured more than 80% of Pb2+.
evidence_result.evidence_span: alkoxy-poly tetra ethylene glycol was developed as a hole transport layer that could capture >80% of Pb2+

evidence_result.content: With the supramolecular sequestration complex, water Pb concentration stayed within EPA limits after 1 hour even when the film was scratched.
evidence_result.evidence_span: As a result, the Pb concentration in water reached 14 ppb after 1 h (within the 15 ppb limit for drinking water by the US Environmental Protection Agency), even if the perovskite film were scratched214.

evidence_result.content: In the US, recycling costs far exceed recovered material value.
evidence_result.evidence_span: the recycling cost is ~$25 per module, and yet yields materials with a value of only ~$3, depending on recycling efficiency207.

evidence_result.content: UK policy lagged PV deployment, with incentives introduced four years before WEEE regulations, leaving waste financing and reporting unaccounted for.
evidence_result.evidence_span: in the UK, the WEEE regulations came into force in 2014, but government incentives for PVs were introduced in 2010, meaning there were four years of exponential PV deployment in which the financing or reporting of waste volumes were unaccounted for.

evidence_result.content: Recent progress indicates that circularity and performance can improve together via green recycling solvents, Pb sequestration, and regenerative tandem design.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Recent progress shows that circularity and performance can advance in parallel, with developments in green solvent systems (e.g., water-based routes) for Pb recycling, effective sequestration strategies to prevent Pb release, and regenerative tandem designs that allow MHP top-cell replacement.

constraint.content: Sustainable deployment must address separation, critical elements, lead release, manufacturing impacts, recycling steps, and policy.
constraint.evidence_span: These concerns include (i) the practicalities of separating modules to access the active materials for recycling, and whether the devices/materials extracted are of sufficient value for re-use in commercially-competitive modules, (ii) the use of critical elements in the device architecture, (iii) preventing harmful release of Pb-containing compounds to the environment during manufacturing, deployment and EOL, (iv) reducing the energy intensity and environmental impacts of the manufacturing processes, (v) the processing sequences required for recycling, and (vi) policy frameworks ensuring sustainable EOL management, driving mandates for high recovery rates, and fostering resilient supply chains.

constraint.content: Future tandem sustainability requires manufacturing near deployment, low-carbon electricity, local materials, and management or elimination of harmful materials.
constraint.evidence_span: For MHP-based tandems to have improved sustainability credentials compared to current c-Si modules, tandem manufacturing should take place in regions close to deployment, using electricity supplies with relatively low CO2eq sources, and using locally-sourced materials with harmful materials either eliminated or heavily managed at EOL.

constraint.content: High-efficiency tandems should be deployed where they maximize fossil-fuel displacement.
constraint.evidence_span: For the greatest impact on reducing global emissions, high-efficiency PV devices, such as MHP/Si tandems, should be deployed to maximize fossil fuels displacement, for example, in countries with high coal use

constraint.content: Policy should favor new tandem installations or penalize premature c-Si decommissioning.
constraint.evidence_span: Policy must drive incentives for MHP-based tandems to be preferentially used as new installations, or penalizing premature c-Si single-junction PV decommissioning.

constraint.content: Sustainable solar technologies require responsible sourcing, local manufacturing-deployment alignment, transparency, recyclability without sacrificing performance, nearby recycling, and anticipatory policy.
constraint.evidence_span: for future solar technologies to be sustainable, consideration must be given for the responsible sourcing of materials and location of manufacturing in relation to deployment, with traceability and transparency integral for the information provided to consumers. Manufacturers must be incentivized (or regulated) to produce easier-to-recycle technologies, whilst not compromising the longevity or performance, and with recycling undertaken as close to the source of the waste as possible, and a policy framework which preempts and embraces the technological advancements.

constraint.content: The review evaluates elements flagged by hazardous-substance and critical-material frameworks.
constraint.evidence_span: Our analysis focuses on elements that are either flagged in regulatory frameworks, e.g., the European Union’s Restriction of Hazardous Substances (RoHS) directive116, Control of Substances Hazardous to Health (COSHH) or critical raw material lists

constraint.content: A DPR above 20% is treated as a barrier to sustainable terawatt-scale deployment.
constraint.evidence_span: DPR > 20% signals a barrier to sustainable TWp-scale deployment120.

constraint.content: Cs use in wide-bandgap perovskites is limited at terawatt scale by supply constraints.
constraint.evidence_span: Although Cs is a minor component by mass (2-5 wt%) in perovskite films, it is constrained at the TW-scale by an average DPR of 1468%.

constraint.content: Inorganic transport layers in tandems must be compatible with temperature- and solvent-sensitive underlying stacks.
constraint.evidence_span: However, tandems have limited selection of inorganic transporting layers, because, especially for 2-T tandems, layers must be deposited using processes that are compatible with the underlying device stack.

constraint.content: c-Si bottom cells impose an upper thermal budget below about 200–250 °C.
constraint.evidence_span: c-Si bottom cells employing amorphous-Si passivation or TCO layers imposes upper thermal limit of < 200–250 °C

constraint.content: Deposition on MHP bottom cells must avoid polar solvents, high-temperature annealing, and sputtering, favoring solvent-free processes.
constraint.evidence_span: Depositing on MHP bottom cells must avoid polar solvents, high-temperature annealing, and sputtering, therefore the chosen materials should be compatible with solvent-free processes e.g., atomic layer deposition, evaporation, dry transfer139.

constraint.content: Tandem electrode deposition must avoid damaging perovskite absorbers and temperature-sensitive Si passivation layers.
constraint.evidence_span: In tandem devices, electrode deposition must also avoid damaging the perovskite absorber or disrupting the temperature-sensitive passivation layers used in c-Si bottom cells.

constraint.content: Even low-temperature ZnO-based TCOs still face sputter-damage compatibility issues with MHP and amorphous-Si layers.
constraint.evidence_span: These materials are generally more compatible with tandem processing because they can be deposited at lower temperatures, although sputter damage to MHP layers and amorphous Si passivation layers for c-Si remains a challenge.

constraint.content: Physical encapsulation barriers can fail under catastrophic events like hail, so additional lead-release prevention is needed.
constraint.evidence_span: But these physical barriers can be broken during deployment, for example through hail. Strategies to prevent Pb release in the event of a catastrophic failure of encapsulation are essential

constraint.content: Operational lifetime uncertainty affects sustainability, economics, and the timing of end-of-life recycling or repurposing.
constraint.evidence_span: the operational lifetime of MHP/Si tandems is not currently well-established, and lifetime impacts sustainability and economic metrics whilst also influencing when there will be significant end of life modules that require recycling or repurposing.

constraint.content: Recycling needs full manufacturer disclosure of materials, potentially enabled by legislation.
constraint.evidence_span: Identifying the materials ahead of recycling requires a full breakdown available from the manufacturer. Legislation could enable this by requiring a breakdown of materials used in PV panels to be available.

constraint.content: Future lead-sequestration strategies should be scalable, low-temperature, low-solvent, and validated under realistic conditions.
constraint.evidence_span: future efforts should focus on developing high-capacity sequestration strategies that can readily be integrated into modules with scalable, low-temperature, low-solvent approaches, and validated under realistic mechanical, environmental, and cycling conditions

constraint.content: Recyclability, critical-material substitution, and lead-risk management should be treated as first-order design constraints alongside efficiency and durability.
constraint.evidence_span: By treating recyclability, critical-material substitution, and lead risk management as first-order design constraints, alongside the more widely-studied efficiency and durability metrics

contradiction.content: Literature reports conflict on whether released Pb from perovskites is severe or immobilized in soil.
contradiction.evidence_span: there remains debate about how severe the release of Pb would be. Whilst some studies have indicated that plants grown in soil contaminated with 250 mg kg-1 Pb2+ from MHP films exhibits orders of magnitude increases in their Pb content202, other works indicate that Pb2+ should be immobilized in soil203.

contradiction.content: Some design goals conflict, such as stronger encapsulation for Pb control versus easier delamination for recycling.
contradiction.evidence_span: There are significant technical challenges, and some are contradictory. For example, improving encapsulation to prevent Pb release to the waste stream can also make delamination of glass more difficult.

contradiction.content: Design goals can conflict at end of life: longevity-enhancing design may make modules harder to recycle.
contradiction.evidence_span: design for longevity can make the module more difficult to recycle

contradiction.content: Some sustainability improvements in manufacturing can worsen recycling outcomes, and vice versa.
contradiction.evidence_span: Methods to reduce the environmental impact of producing MHP-based tandems can be both positive and negative for recycling at EOL.

problem_motivation.content: As PV deployment scales to multi-terawatt levels, urgent sustainability problems must be addressed across the lifecycle, including resource depletion, energy/carbon-intensive production, waste management, and material circularity.
evidence_spans: As photovoltaics (PVs) scale from one to multiple terawatts over the next decade, ensuring sustainable deployment is urgently required.
But with this rapid growth, there are urgent sustainability challenges, particularly regarding the management of PV waste and the circularity of materials used in solar modules
the depletion of critical resources (especially silver, indium, copper), energy- and carbon-intensive production, and EOL waste management, remain unaddressed for multi-TWₚ-scale PV deployment

problem_motivation.content: Current c-Si PVs already pose major sustainability and recycling problems that tandem technologies may inherit, so stability, durability qualification, and recycling infrastructure must advance to avoid repeating c-Si waste, resource, and design constraints.
evidence_spans: Crystalline silicon (c-Si) PVs, the current industry standard, will generate an estimated 160 million tonnes of waste by 2050, and there remains complex technoeconomic challenges associated with their recycling.
we begin the review by discussing the sustainability challenges in the c-Si PV supply chain, which will remain in place for perovskite/c-Si tandems, and have to be addressed

Stability targets, durability qualification, and recycling infrastructures must evolve alongside efficiency improvements to avoid repeating the waste, resource, and design constraints faced by c-Si PV.

problem_motivation.content: A central motivation for perovskite/tandem PV sustainability work is that commercialization of promising lab results requires solving critical circularity challenges, especially sustainable materials selection, scalable recycling and reuse, stack delamination, prevention of lead release, and supportive lifecycle policy.
evidence_spans: At this pivotal juncture when perovskite PVs begin to enter the market, this review examines the critical circularity challenges that must be addressed: substitution of scarce raw materials, scalable recycling protocols, cost-effective stack delamination, safe lead sequestration, and policy frameworks to encourage circularity across the device lifecycle with effective incentives.
Nevertheless, realizing these benefits and demonstrations made in the lab to commercial advantages requires addressing several key factors

we examine strategies to enhance the sustainability of perovskite-based tandem solar cells, focusing on three critical challenges: the development of In-free transparent electrodes, the recycling and reuse of materials, and prevention of lead release during PV deployment.
many engineering challenges remain

problem_motivation.content: Environmental risks of MHP-based tandems must be evaluated at multi-terawatt scale despite their potential circularity benefits, because the technology remains commercially immature and still faces technical and manufacturing challenges.
evidence_spans: Whilst MHP-based tandems offer appealing opportunities to improve PV circularity and lower the overall environmental footprint per unit energy produced, it is critical to evaluate the environmental risks when tandems are deployed on the multi-TWp scale.
MHP-based tandems are still at an early commercial stage but shows great promise in overcoming these technical and manufacturing challenges72,99,102.

problem_motivation.content: Materials selection is a major sustainability bottleneck for tandem PVs because high-performance devices rely on scarce or supply-risk elements—especially indium in ITO/TCEs, but also Ag, Au, and Cs—creating supply-chain and scalability concerns and motivating In-free transparent conductors and recovery strategies.
evidence_spans: Most high-efficiency MHP-based tandems use lead-based absorbers and indium-based TCEs, raising environmental and supply-chain concerns
However, In, classified as a critical raw material, has limited global reserves and its production is energy-intensive, as it is primarily produced as a byproduct of Zn mining

If MHP PVs are to be deployed at the TW-scale, it will be challenging for the PV industry to afford virgin In. Therefore, diversifying away from In in TCOs, combined with developing recovery strategies for ITO/glass substrates are urgent strategic priorities123.
Motivated by the need for more sustainable and scalable alternatives to ITO in tandem photovoltaics
the reliance of these TCEs on scarce indium with high DPR motivates the development of more sustainable alternatives
materials selection emerges as a central sustainability challenge, particularly due to the reliance on elements with high depletion potential or supply risk, such as In, Ag, Au, and Cs.
In, widely used in TCOs, faces both geological scarcity and competing demands from display technologies, motivating the development of In-free transparent conductors.

problem_motivation.content: Lead use is a fundamental sustainability concern for perovskite tandems: the inherent neurotoxicity of Pb motivates prevention of lead release, but key uncertainties remain about how long sequestration materials remain effective, requiring longer-term study.
evidence_spans: A critical factor to address is the inherent use of neurotoxic Pb in lead-halide perovskites.
an important question with all of these approaches is how long these sequestration materials are effective for before all functional sites are saturated.
Longer-term studies are therefore important to evaluate and guide the future development of effective Pb sequestration materials.

problem_motivation.content: Recycling and circular manufacturing for tandem/perovskite PVs remain unresolved because practical end-of-life separation is difficult and insufficiently characterized, including poorly quantified clean delamination energy demands, difficult separation of SnI2 and PbI2 in all-perovskite tandems, and the lack of demonstrated closed-loop manufacturing.
evidence_spans: the energy intensity needed for ‘clean’ delamination and separation of the module into its constituent parts56,57 is currently not well quantified
However, separating the SnI2 and PbI2 salts from all-perovskite tandems is challenging, given that both Pb-only and Pb/Sn perovskites dissolve in the same polar solvents.
Closed-loop manufacturing of all-perovskite tandems has not yet been demonstrated because of this challenge

problem_motivation.content: Device lifetime uncertainty is a sustainability concern for tandems because MHP layers may degrade and reach end of life before the c-Si subcell, complicating durability, refurbishment, and circularity strategies.
evidence_spans: In comparison, the longevity of MHPs is less certain due to the nascency of this technology, creating an inherent sustainability challenge that the MHP cell may reach EOL years before the c-Si cell.
further work is needed to ensure recycled modules match the highest-performance modules manufactured in specialist facilities.

problem_motivation.content: Policy and standards are a major unmet prerequisite for sustainable tandem deployment: existing PV frameworks do not adequately cover MHP tandems, consumers cannot objectively compare environmental credentials, and new MHP-specific regulation, stability standards, eco-design incentives, traceability, and end-of-life governance are urgently needed before wide deployment.
evidence_spans: Upon widescale deployment of these tandems, under the existing global PV framework, consumers would not be able to objectively compare environmental credentials of c-Si with MHP-based technologies.

Without enforced regulation and globally recognized standards of reused modules, there is a risk that unsafe or damaged modules which have reached EoL will be transported to developing regions without adequate local recycling facilities.

There must be a significant change in the global policy frameworks in order to support a future scenario which has design for disassembly and profitable and responsible end of life policies at its heart.

There is an urgency to pre-empt developing effective policy before MHP-based tandems are widely deployed, recognizing there is typically a delay between rapidly emerging technologies entering the market and regulations entering into legislation and adoption.
the first question that needs to be addressed is which policy framework will regulate the MHP sector.
The integration of more complex material compositions, MHP cell structures, and more durable encapsulants will require a new approach as to how perovskites are regulated.
The degradation mechanisms of MHPs are not yet well understood, and this uncertainty will impact on policy.

the existing IEC standards for stability tests of PV devices are designed for conventional solar panels based on c-Si, GaAs, CIGS, or CdTe. However, MHPs have different device architectures and specific material properties and therefore, a new standard stability test should be established for MHPs under illumination, heat, and bias voltage232.

the development of a responsible and coherent policy framework is most effectively implemented by the perovskite sector itself via voluntary standards with self-preserving interests. However, by virtue of being voluntary does not guarantee compliance.
policy frameworks developed for legacy PV technologies must adapt to the distinct material flows and risks of MHP tandems, incentivizing eco-design and full material traceability.

problem_motivation.content: Reuse and second-life pathways for tandem modules are attractive but currently constrained by practical and market barriers such as certification, warranties, transport, and uncertainty over whether refurbished modules can match top-tier manufacturing performance.
evidence_spans: further work is needed to ensure recycled modules match the highest-performance modules manufactured in specialist facilities.
there are many barriers preventing reuse, such as warranties, transport and certification.

problem_motivation.content: Some sustainability-motivated materials substitutions also remain immature: replacing expensive, environmentally impactful organic charge-transport layers and moving to alternative contacts is desirable, but lifecycle data and reliability performance are still incomplete.
evidence_spans: There is therefore strong motivation to replace these charge transport layers with more cost-effective and more stable metal oxide HTLs (e.g., NiOx and MoO3) and ETLs (TiO2, SnO2, etc).
Although no full LCA of SAM-based contacts has yet been published
but requires advances in corrosion resistance, contact resistivity, and long-term reliability.

prior_approach.content: Previous reviews mainly focused on manufacturing sustainability or single-junction perovskites, rather than the broader tandem-specific issues discussed here.
evidence_spans: previous reviews that focus primarily on manufacturing sustainability or single-junction perovskites30,34–41

prior_approach.content: Prior work on scalable fabrication for tandems has explored alternative large-area deposition methods, including thermal co-evaporation, hybrid evaporation-solution processing, and slot-die/meniscus coating, to achieve uniform, defect-free films on textured silicon wafers.
evidence_spans: alternative methods are under development to achieve uniform, defect-free film deposition over large-area, textured silicon wafer bottom cells94–96, such as through thermal co‑evaporation, a combination of evaporation and solution processing, and scalable meniscus-coating techniques like slot‑die coating97,98

prior_approach.content: Earlier life-cycle assessments suggested that, if stability, precursor utilization, and manufacturing yield are improved, perovskite/silicon tandems could have lower embodied energy and faster energy payback than single-junction c-Si; prior LCAs also consistently identified the c-Si wafer as the dominant embodied-energy contributor.
evidence_spans: early life-cycle assessments already suggest that these processing advantages could offer reduced embodied energy and faster payback times than single-junction c-Si PV when combined with improved device stability, precursor utilization efficiency, and manufacturing yield99
consistent with prior LCAs (Box 3)88

prior_approach.content: Prior recycling and regeneration studies for MHP/Si tandems reported removing degraded perovskite top cells to restore the c-Si bottom cell and enable tandem refurbishment: one reported two-step protocol used thermal delamination at about 180 °C followed by selective chemical cleaning to recover the silicon sub-cell, after which a new MHP top cell could be redeposited.
evidence_spans: A two-step protocol was reported recovering the c-Si bottom cell from a degraded MHP/Si tandem: thermal delamination at approximately 180 °C to soften the encapsulant and mechanically separating the top MHP sub-cell from the bottom c-Si wafer, followed by selective chemical cleaning to strip residual interlayers106.

The lower stability of MHPs compared with c-Si has led some researchers to investigate methods of removing the MHP cell from a degraded MHP/Si tandem to bring the silicon cell back to its original performance106 and allow a new MHP cell to be deposited, regenerating the tandem.

prior_approach.content: Prior recycling approaches for perovskite and tandem devices have often followed single-junction MHP strategies, focusing on reuse of ITO-coated glass, recovery of Pb as PbI2, and solvent recycling; reported methods include multi-solvent baths that selectively dissolve functional layers and recover HTLs such as spiro-OMeTAD, as well as water-based processes with additives and temperature control that recover PbI2, Au, SnO2, Spiro-OMeTAD, and ITO-glass. Solution-based recovery methods have also shown potential to yield high-quality recycled perovskite materials.
evidence_spans: MHP/MHP tandems are generally considered to have similar recycling method as single cell MHP solar cell, where the focus is reusing ITO-coated glass, recovery of Pb as PbI2, and recycling organic solvents108

Multi-solvent chemical baths can selectively dissolve the functional layers. HTL materials, e.g., 2,2’,7,7’-tetrakis(N,N-di-p-methoxyphenylamine)-9,9’-spirobifluorene (spiro-OMeTAD), soluble in non-polar solvents, have been recycled using chlorobenzene

Water-based recycling methods using specific additives (sodium acetate, sodium iodide, and hypophosphorous acid) and temperature control have been reported to recover functional layers, including lead(II) iodide (PbI2), gold (Au), Tin oxide (SnO2), Spiro-OMeTAD, and the ITO-coated glass23,24
work undertaken to develop solution-based methods for recovering perovskite materials has shown there is potential to produce high quality recycled materials

prior_approach.content: Prior materials and device-design work had already demonstrated several component choices relevant to tandems, including Cs-free wide-bandgap perovskite top cells, rubidium A-site passivation, and widespread use of FTO as a robust transparent conducting oxide, especially in silicon bottom cells and tandem architectures.
evidence_spans: Whilst Cs-free WBG MHPs are available for the tandem top cell
Rubidium (Rb) has also been used in the A-site of the perovskite for passivation134
Fluorine-doped tin oxide (FTO) has also been widely used as a TCO due to its thermal and chemical robustness, particularly in silicon bottom cells and tandem device architectures179.

prior_approach.content: Alternative prior lead-mitigation strategies included designing charge-transport layers or using bulk additives that can sequester Pb.
evidence_spans: Alternative approaches include making the charge transport layers capable of sequestering Pb.

prior_limitation.content: Current c-Si PV recycling infrastructure and economics recover only a small fraction of valuable materials because there is a shortage of cost-effective facilities, and present panel volumes make centralized recycling unprofitable relative to recovered value.
evidence_spans: Despite silicon and precious metals like silver (Ag) being valuable resources, only 15–20% of these materials are recovered from end-of-life (EOL) modules
there is a shortage of recycling facilities that can extract the full value from silicon panels cost effectively.

This limitation is mainly due to the current small volumes of solar panels making centralised recycling facilities unprofitable, such that recycling is not cost effective compared with the value of materials recovered224,225.

prior_limitation.content: Existing EPR/WEEE policy frameworks are poorly aligned with circularity: they do not incentivize design for circularity or mandate adequate eco-design, disclosure of embedded materials, or recycling methods; they place recycling burdens downstream; and they often fail to account for differences among PV technologies.
evidence_spans: Under the existing Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR) framework, PV producers are not incentivized to design for circularity

EPR does not mandate adequate eco-design strategies (‘upstream’), instead placing the burden of creating technoeconomic solutions for recycling at end-of-life (‘downstream’) on future generations to resolve. EPR does not mandate PV manufacturers to release information of embedded materials or recycling methods.

The existing EPR and WEEE regulations do not account for variations in solar PV cell types (e.g., CIGS, CdTe, c-Si), which are viewed ubiquitously in the policy framework, despite diverging characteristics, degradation modes, and EOL pathways229.

prior_limitation.content: Policy and waste regulation lag technological progress: development, ratification, implementation, enforcement, and standards recognition are too slow, often leaving regulation outdated by the time it takes effect.
evidence_spans: the timeframe for policy to be implemented and international standards to be recognized that would alleviate sustainability challenges for PV technologies is a concern compared to the speed at which the technology itself is advancing
the speed at which policy is developed and ratified rarely keeps pace with technological advancements
Waste regulation is typically slow to be enforced in relation to the pace of technological change, rendering it outdated by the time it is implemented.

prior_limitation.content: PV policy effectiveness is limited by jurisdictional variation, mismatch between manufacturer locality and global markets, and dependence on enforcement; in practice, producers may freeride on financing responsibilities.
evidence_spans: Policy is limited by variations in geographic jurisdiction and the conflict between the locality of the manufacturer and the global market.
However, EPR relies on enforcement by the authorities to be properly enacted, and there is evidence that PV producers are ‘freeriding’64 their responsibilities to finance EPR

prior_limitation.content: Lead-free perovskite alternatives remain limited because they underperform Pb-based systems in efficiency and stability and may not actually reduce environmental impacts once lower yields and shorter lifetimes are considered.
evidence_spans: these alternatives currently lag behind in efficiency and (for Sn-based perovskites) stability compared to Pb-halide perovskite systems89–92, and do not necessarily have lower environmental impacts as a result of these lower energy yields and device lifetime93

prior_limitation.content: Lab-scale spin-coated MHP tandem manufacturing does not scale well to gigawatt production, with throughput, yield, and reproducibility still limiting scalability and therefore lifetime, energy output, and environmental performance.
evidence_spans: Lab-scale (spin coated) solution-based manufacturing of MHP-based tandems does not scale to gigawatt-level production94

production throughput, yield, and reproducibility continue to limit scalability, which in turn affects device lifetime and energy output, and therefore critically influence overall life-cycle environmental performance94

prior_limitation.content: Some proposed recycling routes remain technically limited: chlorobenzene-based HTL recycling did not remove dopants, while polar-solvent perovskite dissolution relies on hazardous solvents and shows limited selectivity across different device stacks.
evidence_spans: although dopants such as cobalt-bis(trifluoromethanesulfonyl)imide (Co-TFSI) were not removed by the process107

The perovskite layers can be dissolved by polar organic solvents, such N,N-dimethylformamide (DMF) or methylamine, although the hazardous solvents pose environmental risks and exhibit limited selectivity across diverse device stacks.

prior_limitation.content: Current LCAs for MHP tandems are still preliminary and biased toward high-efficiency lab devices, often using narrow system boundaries that omit BOS, transport, and end-of-life impacts.
evidence_spans: It is crucial to recognize that due to the low technology readiness level of MHP-based. tandems, current LCAs are preliminary and often biased towards high-PCE laboratory devices. Most assessments have narrow system boundaries, excluding the impacts of balance-of-system components (inverters, wiring), transportation, and end-of-life processing, which are all vital for a complete environmental profile.

prior_limitation.content: Interconnection and contact-material options remain inadequate: sub-10-nm ITO layers can cause resistive losses and interfacial damage; no current alternative matches ITO across key performance and manufacturability metrics; tin-based oxide use in tandems remains limited; FTO requires high deposition temperatures that can damage tandem layers; AZO/GZO face resistivity, deposition-damage, interface-defect, and stability problems; and non-In TCO alternatives still struggle with stability, interface compatibility, and scalable low-temperature processing.
evidence_spans: sub-10-nm ITO layers often introduce resistive losses and interfacial damage that degrade device performance124
however, no single alternative yet combines the optical transparency, low resistivity, environmental stability, surface uniformity, and industrial maturity of ITO176–178.
their implementation in tandem devices remains limited.

high deposition temperatures (>400 °C)185 can degrade perovskite layers and charge-transport materials, limiting the applicability of FTO-type electrodes in monolithic tandem architectures, particularly as top contacts.

Nevertheless, lower carrier mobility (15-30 cm2 V–1 s–1) compared to ITO limits the ability to reduce the resistivity (Figure 3b)195,196, and challenges remain in depositing these films without damaging underlying perovskite layers, managing interface defects, and ensuring long-term thermal and moisture stability187.
Yet challenges persist in these alternatives, including stability under illumination and heat, interfacial compatibility with MHP and silicon, and scalable, low-temperature processing.

prior_limitation.content: Some perovskite composition/interface strategies remain constrained: existing Cs-free wide-bandgap perovskites suffer instability and high defect density, while rubidium-based passivation faces supply-chain constraints and high cost.
evidence_spans: they suffer from instability and high defect densities, necessitating further advancements in composition engineering and interface passivation133
but faces fundamental supply chain constraints and prohibitive costs134

prior_limitation.content: Tandem regeneration/reuse approaches may be technically feasible at lab scale, but their economic viability remains uncertain.
evidence_spans: Whilst this can work for lab-based cells, the economics of this process need to be further explored

prior_limitation.content: Module disassembly and reuse are hindered because cost-effective frame removal can crack toughened glass, and delamination can break glass or cells, reducing reuse potential.
evidence_spans: Removing the aluminium frames in a cost-effective manner, which usually takes place before delamination, can cause the chemically toughened glass to crack, reducing any opportunity for reuse in a panel.
Delamination of the module, which is a common challenge for Si modules and MHP/Si modules, can further complicate reuse if the glass or cells are broken35.

prior_limitation.content: Reuse of patterned transparent conducting electrodes is limited because module-specific conducting patterns may change over time, requiring as-yet undeveloped repair or pattern-adjustment methods for reused glass.
evidence_spans: for the TCE to be valuable for future reuse, methods of repairing / adjusting the conducting pattern on reused glass would need to be developed.

prior_limitation.content: Second-life and refurbishment markets face major barriers: a trust gap around invisible defects reduces confidence in performance and yield; consumer concerns and aesthetics matter; cheaper, better new modules compete strongly; and refurbished MHP/Si tandems may face even greater barriers because high-performance reuse requires complete removal of MHP and residues from the Si bottom cell.
evidence_spans: c-Si panels, when decommissioned for repowering, face significant barriers to entering second-life markets217, primarily driven by a ‘trust gap’ regarding panel performance. The invisible defects of the reused panels will lower module efficiencies and production yield

there are often secondary concerns, such as aesthetics which influence consumer behaviour207. Furthermore, the solar reuse market is competing with the decreasing costs of newer modules with increasing generation outputs226.

Reused or refurbished MHP/Si modules are likely to encounter similar issues, or face greater challenges because high-performance tandems require complete removal of the MHP and organic residue from the c-Si bottom cell.

prior_limitation.content: Manufacturer-managed takeback schemes are risky if the supplying company fails or mishandles end-of-life obligations, implying the need for external oversight.
evidence_spans: there is a risk with the ‘First Solar’ model if the company supplying the future MHP-based tandem modules runs into administration or mishandles their EOL responsibilities or finances, it is appropriate that an inter-governmental watchdog monitors or has oversight over this type of scheme.

rejected_alternative.content: Previous review framings focused mainly on manufacturing sustainability or single-junction perovskites, rather than an integrated circularity perspective tailored to tandem PVs.
evidence_spans: In contrast to previous reviews that focus primarily on manufacturing sustainability or single-junction perovskites30,34–41, we provide an integrated assessment of circularity strategies tailored specifically to tandem PVs

rejected_alternative.content: 4-T tandems, despite some recycling advantages, are not the preferred commercialization pathway; efforts favor 2-T tandems because they require less demanding transparent conducting electrodes, have lower optical losses and higher efficiency limits, and avoid additional inverters and related balance-of-system costs.

evidence_spans: The thin interconnection layer (ICL) is not considered for recycling due to the low mass percentage and lower chances of selective removal of individual MHP layer followed by cost-effective separation of high-purity critical materials.

rejected_alternative.content: High-temperature TiO2 or NiOx layers are unsuitable for direct use in these tandems because the c-Si bottom cell cannot tolerate the required thermal budget.
evidence_spans: which limits the direct use of high-temperature TiO2 or NiOx layers
