causal_claim.content: Complex and contamination-prone PV panel compositions lead to disposal or downgraded repurposing/reuse rather than true closed-loop recycling, limiting circularity and continuing environmental harms; these recycling challenges already seen in c-Si are expected to be amplified in MHP/Si devices.
evidence_spans: As a result, many panels in the USA are disposed of via landfill, while in Europe they are often repurposed, for instance, as building aggregates in roads, in ways that limit true materials circularity and continue to pose environmental challenges
due to contamination, this glass is typically downgraded to cement or aggregates with reduced environmental benefits compared to recycling glass back to sheet
the engineering issues that currently trouble c-Si PV about differences in panel composition, low material value and difficulties in delamination will be amplified with MHP/Si devices

causal_claim.content: Multi-junction/tandem architectures can exceed single-junction c-Si efficiency limits because they combine complementary absorbers that capture different parts of the solar spectrum.
evidence_spans: Multi-junction devices combine sub-cells absorbing in complementary parts of the solar spectrum, raising theoretical efficiency limits well beyond the practical limit of single-junction c-Si PVs

causal_claim.content: Higher tandem efficiency and energy yield produce more electricity per unit area and per material/energy input, which lowers environmental impact per kWh and can reduce balance-of-system needs, land use, lifecycle greenhouse-gas emissions, embodied energy, and energy payback time relative to single-junction c-Si.
evidence_spans: These efficiency gains translate into higher energy yield per unit area, which therefore lowers the environmental impact per kWh generated.

the higher energy yield in MHP-based tandem PVs translates directly into sustainability benefits by delivering more electricity per manufacturing energy and material input than conventional c-Si PVs, thereby reducing balance-of-system requirements, land use, and lifecycle greenhouse gas emissions per unit power generated
Owing to the low temperature processability of the MHP top-cell, perovskite-silicon tandems can achieve shorter energy payback times and lower embodied energy than single-junction c-Si PVs

causal_claim.content: Replacing c-Si with thin-film perovskite-based absorbers can reduce carbon and energy burdens and ease recycling challenges because perovskites use less material, can be processed at low temperature, and have largely solvent-soluble functional layers that may enable simpler, cheaper recycling routes.
evidence_spans: Replacing the c-Si cell can allow MHP-based tandems to overcome the challenges inherent to c-Si modules, such as its high carbon dioxide equivalent (CO2eq) footprint, high energy cost of production, and challenging and costly recycling.
perovskite cells require lower material use than c-Si cells, and can be processed via low-temperature methods that enable reduced CO2eq footprints during manufacture

the functional layers in MHP cells are largely soluble in relatively mild solvents, which opens up recycling routes for the MHP cell(s)23,24 that are potentially simpler and more cost-effective than c-Si recycling

causal_claim.content: Combining tandem efficiency with thin-film, low-temperature perovskite processing creates sustainability and deployment opportunities, including lighter modules that are easier to integrate into buildings and cheaper to install.
evidence_spans: Such MHP-based tandem technologies combine the high efficiency potential of tandem architectures with the low-temperature processing and thin-film material use characteristic of perovskite absorbers, creating opportunities to meet performance requirements while delivering sustainability improvements.

all-thin film tandems thus enable low-weight, high-specific-power modules manufactured via low-temperature processes that facilitate easier integration into existing building structures and reduce installation costs

causal_claim.content: Optimized MHP/Si tandems can deliver substantially higher real-world annual energy yield than single-junction c-Si, aided in warm climates by perovskites' lower temperature coefficient; tailoring bandgap and thickness to location can further maximize output and improve material utilization.
evidence_spans: Optimized MHP/Si PV systems can achieve annual energy yields (electrical energy produced by PVs, in kWh, in real-world scenarios)81 up to 30% higher than single-junction c-Si PVs under real-world conditions82.

perovskites exhibit a lower temperature coefficient (typically –0.15% to –0.3% °C–1  vs. silicon's –0.4% to –0.5% °C–1), providing a relative advantage for perovskite-based devices in warmer conditions

By tailoring the design of perovskite solar cells, primarily through bandgap tuning (e.g., via compositional changes) and absorber layer thickness optimization87, to specific locations and operating conditions, it is possible to maximize their energy output and achieve improved material utilization ratios

causal_claim.content: Short service life or premature retirement can negate tandem sustainability gains and increase waste: early failure of the MHP sub-cell, repowering driven by higher efficiency, or replacement of still-working c-Si systems with tandem modules can accelerate PV waste growth unless reuse/recycling solutions and policy intervention are in place.
evidence_spans: Premature EOL of the MHP sub-cell could negate the overall sustainability benefits gained from the transition to tandems with MHPs, and have the potential to exacerbate exponential c-Si waste volumes expected during this period, unless effective methods for recycling the c-Si bottom cell are developed.

an unintended consequence of transitioning from single-junction c-Si PV to MHP-based tandems is that older, working c-Si systems are prematurely decommissioned and replaced with newer tandem modules, further accelerating waste volumes unless viable c-Si reuse markets can be established

Without policy intervention, MHP-based tandems are likely to shorten the lifetime of current single junction PV in countries with strong incentives for low carbon electricity generation and lower carbon emissions
technological developments (such as increased efficiency) can lead to ‘repowering’ and early retirement of modules after less than 10 years operation.

causal_claim.content: Extending module service life substantially lowers climate impact: increasing lifetime from 10 to 25 years halves GWP without changing energy payback time.
evidence_spans: Extending service life from 10 to 25 years halves GWP while unalters EPBT88,101.

causal_claim.content: Transporting bulky, heavy panels to centralized recycling infrastructure increases total emissions through added hidden CO2eq cost.
evidence_spans: The transportation of bulky, heavy c-Si and MHP tandem panels to the centralized PV recycling infrastructure also adds a hidden CO2eq cost to the total emissions

causal_claim.content: 4-terminal tandems are easier to recycle because independently fabricated, mechanically stacked sub-cells can be separated at end of life, whereas monolithic 2-terminal integration makes recovery of valuable materials much more difficult.
evidence_spans: 4-T tandems offer recycling advantage because each sub-cell is fabricated independently and mechanically stacked, allowing for easy separation at EOL of either sub-cell.
Recovering various highly valuable materials from 2-T tandem solar cells is significantly more complicated due to the monolithic integration of the sub-cells.

causal_claim.content: Water-based recovery processes can significantly reduce resource depletion and lower levelized cost of electricity.
evidence_spans: which significantly reduce overall resource depletion and lower the LCOE

causal_claim.content: Indium scarcity, high ITO thickness requirements, and especially the greater number of TCO layers in 4-T tandems increase material demand, causing supply instability, price volatility, and high demand-to-production ratios; reducing layer thickness can mitigate this burden.
evidence_spans: This results in supply instability and price volatility, with costs reaching ~$452/kg122. The high DPRs arise from the scarcity of In, and the relatively thick ITO layers required to have low sheet resistance, which elevates material demands.
A 4-T module requires three or four thick transparent electrode layers (Box 2), increasing the total TCO material requirement to roughly five times that of a 2-T architecture.
A 35%-efficient tandem device with a 10 nm-thick IZO-based ICL can reduce the DPR to about 23%67

causal_claim.content: Even ultrathin gold interconnection layers can sharply raise demand-to-production ratio and primary energy demand, making Au environmentally and economically unattractive.
evidence_spans: An extremely thin Au ICL of 0.4 nm results in a DPR of approximately 1.4% and contributes up to 42% of the total primary energy demand in MHP/MHP tandem devices, making gold an unfavourable option from environmental and economical perspectives.

causal_claim.content: Cross-linked co-SAM interfacial networks improve stability.
evidence_spans: cross-linking mixed functional molecules to form covalently interconnected interfacial networks (i.e., co-SAMs143,144) can lead to improved stability

causal_claim.content: SAM-based hole-transport/interfacial layers are considered more sustainable than conventional polymeric HTLs because they use far less material, and their spontaneous monolayer formation removes the need for hygroscopic dopants, reducing compositional variability.
evidence_spans: they are widely considered more sustainable than using organic charge transport layers because they use orders of magnitude less material, i.e., sub-nanometre SAMs versus conventional >10-nm-thick polymeric PTAA or doped Spiro-OMeTAD HTLs.
Because SAMs spontaneously form ordered monolayers upon solution deposition, they eliminate the need for hygroscopic dopants required in organic HTLs, thereby reducing compositional variability.

causal_claim.content: Halogen-functionalized SAMs improve performance on textured interfaces by enabling uniform coverage, better hole extraction, and defect passivation.
evidence_spans: Using conjugated halogen-functionalized SAMs can achieve uniform coverage on rough pyramidal surfaces, achieving improved hole extraction and effective defect passivation on textured interfaces145.

causal_claim.content: Lower operating current in tandems reduces resistive losses, allowing higher-resistance metallization and supporting silver-lean PV designs.
evidence_spans: tandem cells possess a lower operating current that significantly reduces resistive power losses, making them more tolerant of higher-resistance grids, and encouraging silver-lean PV technologies

causal_claim.content: High deposition temperatures can damage tandem device components by degrading perovskite absorbers and compromising amorphous-silicon passivation layers; lower-temperature, solution-processed hybrid electrodes may therefore facilitate tandem integration.
evidence_spans: the high deposition temperatures can degrade the perovskite absorber and compromise the amorphous silicon passivation layers of the cells.
These hybrid electrodes may facilitate tandem integration by enabling lower-temperature and solution-processed electrode fabrication.

causal_claim.content: Although indium-free tandems may incur an efficiency penalty, that drawback is increasingly compensated by much lower material criticality.
evidence_spans: the ~10% relative efficiency trade-off is increasingly offset by a 90% reduction in material criticality.

causal_claim.content: Photonic curing enables scalable, low-energy processing on heat-sensitive substrates.
evidence_spans: Photonic curing, which uses millisecond light pulses for rapid, low-energy processing, enables scalable, roll-to-roll fabrication on heat-sensitive substrates.

causal_claim.content: Work-function engineering through doping or buffer layers improves both efficiency and long-term stability.
evidence_spans: work function engineering through doping or interfacial buffer layers improves device efficiency and long-term stability.

causal_claim.content: Because perovskites are water-soluble, lead can be released during real-world deployment through water exposure or fire.
evidence_spans: Given the water solubility of MHPs, Pb2+ can readily be released to the environment upon real-world deployment through contact with water, or released in the vapour phase during a fire.

causal_claim.content: Lead-leaching mitigation layers and sequestration chemistries can substantially reduce Pb release: phosphate-buffered functionalized polymer films lowered leached Pb below the US drinking-water limit, and hydroxyl/carboxyl-rich supramolecular complexes sharply reduced leaching by sequestering Pb2+.
evidence_spans: By applying the PFPF, the content of Pb2+ leached into water decreased from 12.39 mg L-1 to 10.1 mg L-1, within the US requirements of <15 mg L-1 for safe drinking water210.
the high density of hydroxyl and carboxyl groups in the supramolecular complex enabled Pb2+ sequestration214, decreasing the Pb leaching rate in flowing water by a factor of 18.

causal_claim.content: Reducing or replacing precious-metal contacts lowers environmental impact and supports large-scale deployment, but also weakens recycling economics because Ag is a major recoverable value stream; thus lower silver content improves deployability while reducing incentives for recycling.
evidence_spans: replacing Ag and Au grids with copper-based contacts or printed carbon electrodes can significantly reduce the environmental impact of the tandem PV module
with the reducing material content per Wp of high-cost material like silver

Reducing the Ag content per panel is important for enabling TW-scale deployment, however, lower Ag content also reduces the economic incentives for recycling panels, as Ag is one of the main high-value materials recovered during PV recycling.

causal_claim.content: Mandatory environmental product declarations would improve transparency for buyers and, if enforced, create a level playing field that incentivizes sustainability-oriented innovation rather than competition based only on efficiency and energy yield.
evidence_spans: Mandatory EPDs would provide greater transparency for the MHP industry to help buyers make informed decisions about the products’ environmental credentials.

If this approach were enforced, this would create a level playing field for all manufacturers to design for sustainability from the outset. Manufacturers would be incentivized to innovate perovskite technologies with decreasing impact on the environment, instead of the current status quo of competing on ever-increasing cell efficiency and energy yield.

causal_claim.content: Perovskite versatility enables integration into many tandem configurations, including with c-Si, CIGSe, kesterite, CdTe, organic, and all-perovskite devices.
evidence_spans: Their versatility supports their integration into diverse tandem configurations, including with c-Si67, copper indium gallium diselenide (CIGSe)68, kesterites69, cadmium telluride (CdTe)70, organic PV71, and all-perovskite combinations22

mechanism_principle.content: The complex multi-layer construction of c-Si panels makes recycling technically and economically difficult.
evidence_spans: The complex construction of c-Si panels, including durable encapsulants and multi-layered assemblies, presents substantial technical and economic barriers to effective recycling

mechanism_principle.content: Premature PV replacement is driven by improved efficiency of newer panels and the reduced cost of PV modules relative to supporting infrastructure.
evidence_spans: This is driven by several factors, especially the increasing efficiency of new panels, and the reduced cost of PV compared with auxiliary infrastructure, such as frames, grid connection, and inverters

mechanism_principle.content: Keeping c-Si modules in operation longer lowers the total embodied carbon footprint across both primary c-Si and secondary MHP supply chains.
evidence_spans: keeping c-Si modules operational for as long as possible reduces the overall embodied CO2eq footprint of the primary c-Si and secondary MHP supply chain

mechanism_principle.content: Environmental benefits of the tandem approach arise from thin printable absorbers, low-temperature fabrication, and avoiding energy-intensive silicon purification; correspondingly, silicon-free tandems have much lower cumulative energy demand because silicon wafer refinement dominates the impacts of Si-based tandems.
evidence_spans: These improvements arise from thin printable absorbers, lower-temperature fabrication for the entire tandem device, and the elimination of energy-intensive silicon purification.

the cumulative energy demand of silicon-free perovskite tandems is nearly six times lower than that of Si-based tandems, a difference attributed almost entirely to the energy-intensive silicon wafer refinement cycle, which dominates the impact of the latter111

mechanism_principle.content: Closed-loop lead recovery is technically feasible because the lead inventory is low and can be managed through encapsulation, sequestration, and existing recycling infrastructure.
evidence_spans: This low material inventory, combined with encapsulation, sequestration and existing industrial recycling infrastructures, makes closed-loop recovery technically feasible.

mechanism_principle.content: For silicon-free tandems, the main remaining carbon/energy impacts come from manufacturing energy use, especially vacuum deposition, plus transparent conducting oxide deposition and encapsulation.
evidence_spans: the main impacts stem from manufacturing energy (notably vacuum deposition steps), deposition of transparent conducting oxides, and encapsulation112–115

mechanism_principle.content: co-SAMs improve stability by suppressing molecular diffusion, interfacial delamination, and chemical degradation under heat and illumination stress.
evidence_spans: by suppressing molecular diffusion, interfacial delamination, and chemical degradation under heat and illumination

mechanism_principle.content: SnO2-based TCOs have lower intrinsic mobility, so they require higher carrier concentrations to achieve low resistivity; this increases free-carrier absorption, shifts the plasma edge into the NIR, and reduces NIR transmission.
evidence_spans: SnO2-based TCOs generally exhibit lower intrinsic mobility, requiring higher carrier concentrations (≥1020-1021 cm-3)180,181 to achieve low resistivity, which enhances free-carrier absorption and shifts the plasma edge into the near-infrared, reducing NIR transmission relative to higher-mobility TCOs182.

mechanism_principle.content: Aliovalent doping in ZnO introduces n-type carriers, and ZnO's low effective electron mass enables higher mobility and conductivity at lower carrier density, thereby improving NIR transparency.
evidence_spans: Substitution of Zn2+ with Al3+ or Ga3+ introduces n-type carriers, while the low effective electron mass (0.24-0.3m0)186 in ZnO supports relatively high mobility and adequate conductivity at lower carrier concentrations, improving near-infrared transparency for optimized GZO films187.

hypothesis_statement.content: A systems-level, coordinated approach integrating materials, technoeconomic, manufacturing, durability, end-of-life, and policy considerations can co-optimize device performance, efficiency, and sustainability and enable environmentally optimal, full-lifecycle-green terawatt-scale MHP tandem deployment.
evidence_spans: By integrating the materials, technoeconomic and policy dimensions that go beyond conventional lifecycle assessments, we outline actionable strategies to co-optimize device performance and sustainability.

sustainable TW-scale deployment requires coordinated advances across the materials used, manufacturing practices, improving the durability of the devices, and end-of-life management, together with an effective international policy framework for incentivizing circularity.
we strongly recommend taking a systems approach to realize the optimal environmental performance of MHP-based tandems.
Designing the devices, standards, and takeback systems together could make future commercial MHP-based tandems green not just in their electricity production, but across their entire lifecycle.

hypothesis_statement.content: MHP-based PV recycling may enable closed-loop material recovery and reduce the environmental footprint of solar energy systems, but this may require keeping perovskite waste separate from conventional c-Si waste streams through dedicated infrastructure, collection streams, and finance mechanisms.
evidence_spans: These recycling processes possible with MHP-based PVs could enable closed-loop material recovery and reduce the environmental footprint of solar energy systems

it may be necessary for MHPs to be kept separate from traditional c-Si waste streams, due to the need to isolate the reusable elements from EOL for producing new panels, and this would require separate infrastructure, collection streams, and finance mechanisms

hypothesis_statement.content: Indium-free transparent conducting oxides, especially ZnO-based TCOs such as AZO and GZO, are promising alternatives that could combine sustainability with efficiency in tandem solar cells.
evidence_spans: Zinc oxide–based TCOs, particularly aluminium-doped zinc oxide (AZO) and gallium-doped zinc oxide (GZO), are promising In-free alternatives.
developing high-performance indium-free TCOs offers a path to combine sustainability with efficiency in tandem solar cells.

hypothesis_statement.content: Hybrid electrodes are a promising route to achieve high performance, stability, and sustainability.
evidence_spans: Another promising route to achieve high performance, stability and sustainability is to develop hybrid electrodes, such as AgNWs embedded within metal oxides or CPs161,197.

hypothesis_statement.content: Lead sequestration is a key strategy for preventing Pb release after encapsulation failure.
evidence_spans: Pb sequestration is a key approach to doing this.

hypothesis_statement.content: An effective policy framework should reflect the global solar market by harmonizing products to meet the most stringent regulations, and MHP manufacturers should provide mandatory Environmental Product Declarations.
evidence_spans: The policy framework should reflect the global nature of the solar market, whereby solar manufacturers operating worldwide standardize their products to meet the most stringent regulations, making them universally compliant227.
It is a recommendation of this paper that MHP manufacturers should provide mandatory Environmental Product Declarations (EPD).

evidence_result.content: Perovskite-based tandems have achieved very high lab efficiencies: laboratory-scale perovskite/Si tandems have surpassed 34% efficiency, reaching 34.85% by mid-2025 (with modules up to 33%), while all-perovskite tandems have reached 30.1%.
evidence_spans: Laboratory-scale demonstration of perovskite/Si tandems with 1 cm2 device area have already surpassed 34% efficiency

By mid-2025, perovskite/Si two-terminal tandem solar cells have achieved record efficiencies of 34.85% (modules up to 33%), surpassing the efficiency limits of single-junction c-Si PVs72. All-perovskite tandems have reached 30.1% power conversion efficiency (PCE)72

evidence_result.content: Lifecycle assessment results indicate that laboratory-scale MHP/Si tandems slightly outperform conventional c-Si PV on median environmental metrics, whereas all-perovskite tandems perform substantially better; this is largely because the c-Si wafer dominates MHP/Si tandem embodied energy (~95%), and replacing the Si bottom cell with a perovskite bottom cell can cut primary energy consumption by >99%.
evidence_spans: the median primary energy demand for a laboratory-scale MHP/Si tandem module is 13 840 MJ kWp–1... this energy demand corresponds to a median energy-payback time (EPBT) of 1.3 years and global warming potential (GWP) of 915 gCO₂eq kWp-1. These are still marginally improved over c-Si single-junction PVs, which have typical values of 1.5 years and 1224 g CO2eq kWp-1, respectively. But switching to all-perovskite tandems substantially reduces both indicators, with median a EPBT of 0.33 years and GHG intensity of 209 gCO2eq kWp-1

our calculations show that the single-crystalline c-Si wafer accounts for ~95% of the total the embodied energy of the tandem (Figure 2c), consistent with prior LCAs (Box 3)88. Since MHP absorbers require orders of magnitude less energy to produce than c-Si, replacing Si with a perovskite bottom cell reduces primary energy consumption by >99%)

evidence_result.content: Industrial pilot lines and outdoor prototypes provide early validation of the favorable environmental assessments and durability claims for these tandem technologies.
evidence_spans: Industrial pilot lines are validating these environmental assessments, and outdoor prototypes already pass standard damp-heat and thermal-cycling industrial tests16.

evidence_result.content: Recovered c-Si cells can be reused in tandems with little performance penalty: tandems built on recovered cells reached 25.7% PCE versus 26.3% for tandems made from fresh cells.
evidence_spans: The tandems built on these recovered c-Si cells show a PCE of 25.7%, which is comparable to those fabricated from the fresh cells (26.3%)106.

evidence_result.content: A key materials sustainability challenge is indium demand: projected demand-production ratios are extremely high at TW scale (average 761% for perovskite-silicon tandems and 440% for all-perovskite tandems), and in all-perovskite tandems the indium in TCOs alone accounts for 24–50% of total primary material energy demand; even a conventional 20 nm ITO interconnection layer in a 25.4% tandem corresponds to an indium DPR of about 70%.
evidence_spans: the projected DPRs of In are on average 761% for perovskite-silicon and 440% for all-perovskite tandems
the In content of the TCO also accounts for 24–50% of the total materials primary energy demand in MHP/MHP tandems

evidence_result.content: Indium-saving transparent conductor alternatives show promising performance-feasibility tradeoffs: AZO and GZO can provide moderate sheet resistance and high visible transmittance, perovskite-silicon tandems with AZO TCEs have exceeded 28% efficiency, and indium-free tandems are nearing 25% efficiency though still below record ITO/IZO-based devices.
evidence_spans: These materials can achieve sheet resistances of 29–62.5 Ω sq⁻¹ and visible transmittance of approximately 83-94%188–192.
Perovskite-silicon tandem cells with AZO-based TCEs have demonstrated PCEs exceeding 28%, close to those achieved using ITO188.

perovskite/silicon tandems utilizing ALD-deposited AZO as an interconnection layer have recently demonstrated sub-cell efficiencies of 24.94%199. While this remains below the record 35.0% achieved with optimized ITO/IZO stacks200)

evidence_result.content: Silver nanowire networks are presented as a feasible indium-saving alternative: at an estimated optimal loading of ~120 mg m–2, they balance transmittance and sheet resistance and correspond to a low silver DPR of 2.1% at 25% PCE.
evidence_spans: The optimal AgNW density for replacing TCOs has been estimated to be approximately 120 mg m–2, balancing high optical transmittance with low sheet resistance198. Assuming a PCE of 25%, this Ag loading corresponds to a DPR of 2.1% ... rendering AgNW networks a highly feasible alternative to alleviate In usage.

evidence_result.content: Lead-leakage mitigation strategies have shown strong results: an alkoxy-poly tetra ethylene glycol hole transport layer captured >80% of Pb2+, and a supramolecular sequestration complex kept water Pb concentration at 14 ppb after 1 hour—even for scratched films—within the US EPA 15 ppb drinking-water limit.
evidence_spans: alkoxy-poly tetra ethylene glycol was developed as a hole transport layer that could capture >80% of Pb2+

As a result, the Pb concentration in water reached 14 ppb after 1 h (within the 15 ppb limit for drinking water by the US Environmental Protection Agency), even if the perovskite film were scratched214.

evidence_result.content: Economic and policy barriers remain for PV circularity: in the US, recycling costs (~$25 per module) greatly exceed recovered material value (~$3), and in the UK PV incentives preceded WEEE regulation by four years, leaving early waste financing and reporting unaccounted for during rapid deployment.
evidence_spans: the recycling cost is ~$25 per module, and yet yields materials with a value of only ~$3, depending on recycling efficiency207.

in the UK, the WEEE regulations came into force in 2014, but government incentives for PVs were introduced in 2010, meaning there were four years of exponential PV deployment in which the financing or reporting of waste volumes were unaccounted for.

evidence_result.content: Repowering with higher-efficiency modules does not necessarily deliver near-term climate benefits: although replacing c-Si single-junction modules can yield financial benefits after about 8 years in some scenarios, CO2eq emissions benefits are typically not realized until around 15 years of service.
evidence_spans: whilst in some scenarios a financial benefit is obtained by replacing c-Si single-junction modules after 8 years of service, a CO2eq emissions benefit (on replacement with higher-efficiency panels) is not typically realized until 15 years of service

evidence_result.content: First-mile transport contributes relatively little to total lifecycle emissions, but its costs can be substantial, especially in remote regions.
evidence_spans: While this CO2eq contribution is relatively small compared to total lifecycle emissions, ‘first-mile’ transport costs to central distribution centres can be high, particularly in remote regions.

evidence_result.content: Recent progress suggests circularity and performance can be improved simultaneously through green solvent systems for Pb recycling, effective Pb sequestration strategies, and regenerative tandem designs that enable MHP top-cell replacement.
evidence_spans: Recent progress shows that circularity and performance can advance in parallel, with developments in green solvent systems (e.g., water-based routes) for Pb recycling, effective sequestration strategies to prevent Pb release, and regenerative tandem designs that allow MHP top-cell replacement.

constraint.content: Sustainable terawatt-scale deployment of MHP/Si tandems is constrained by a broad set of lifecycle and policy requirements: modules must be designed for practical separation and recycling, reduce manufacturing energy and impacts, minimize or substitute critical materials, prevent harmful Pb release during manufacturing, deployment, failure, and end-of-life, and be supported by policy frameworks that ensure disclosure, high recovery rates, resilient supply chains, and anticipatory regulation.
evidence_spans: These concerns include (i) the practicalities of separating modules to access the active materials for recycling, and whether the devices/materials extracted are of sufficient value for re-use in commercially-competitive modules, (ii) the use of critical elements in the device architecture, (iii) preventing harmful release of Pb-containing compounds to the environment during manufacturing, deployment and EOL, (iv) reducing the energy intensity and environmental impacts of the manufacturing processes, (v) the processing sequences required for recycling, and (vi) policy frameworks ensuring sustainable EOL management, driving mandates for high recovery rates, and fostering resilient supply chains.

Identifying the materials ahead of recycling requires a full breakdown available from the manufacturer. Legislation could enable this by requiring a breakdown of materials used in PV panels to be available.
By treating recyclability, critical-material substitution, and lead risk management as first-order design constraints, alongside the more widely-studied efficiency and durability metrics)

constraint.content: Improved sustainability requires manufacturing to be aligned with deployment: tandems should be produced close to where they are deployed, ideally using low-carbon electricity, locally sourced and responsibly sourced materials, with traceability and transparency for consumers, and with recycling undertaken as close as possible to the waste source.
evidence_spans: For MHP-based tandems to have improved sustainability credentials compared to current c-Si modules, tandem manufacturing should take place in regions close to deployment, using electricity supplies with relatively low CO2eq sources, and using locally-sourced materials with harmful materials either eliminated or heavily managed at EOL.

for future solar technologies to be sustainable, consideration must be given for the responsible sourcing of materials and location of manufacturing in relation to deployment, with traceability and transparency integral for the information provided to consumers. Manufacturers must be incentivized (or regulated) to produce easier-to-recycle technologies, whilst not compromising the longevity or performance, and with recycling undertaken as close to the source of the waste as possible, and a policy framework which preempts and embraces the technological advancements.

constraint.content: Deployment and policy should maximize climate benefit while avoiding wasteful replacement: high-efficiency tandems should be deployed where they displace the most fossil-fuel generation, and policy should favor new tandem installations or penalize premature decommissioning of existing c-Si modules.
evidence_spans: For the greatest impact on reducing global emissions, high-efficiency PV devices, such as MHP/Si tandems, should be deployed to maximize fossil fuels displacement, for example, in countries with high coal use
Policy must drive incentives for MHP-based tandems to be preferentially used as new installations, or penalizing premature c-Si single-junction PV decommissioning.

constraint.content: Material criticality is a deployment constraint: the review treats elements flagged by hazardous-substance and critical-material frameworks as key constraints, with DPR > 20% indicating a barrier to sustainable TW-scale deployment; under this criterion, Cs in wide-bandgap perovskites is supply-constrained at terawatt scale.
evidence_spans: Our analysis focuses on elements that are either flagged in regulatory frameworks, e.g., the European Union’s Restriction of Hazardous Substances (RoHS) directive116, Control of Substances Hazardous to Health (COSHH) or critical raw material lists
DPR > 20% signals a barrier to sustainable TWp-scale deployment120.
Although Cs is a minor component by mass (2-5 wt%) in perovskite films, it is constrained at the TW-scale by an average DPR of 1468%.

constraint.content: Tandem fabrication is constrained by strict process compatibility with sensitive underlying stacks: inorganic transport layers and electrodes must be deposited without damaging perovskite absorbers or temperature-sensitive Si passivation layers, with c-Si bottom cells imposing a thermal budget below about 200–250 °C; deposition on MHP bottom cells must avoid polar solvents, high-temperature annealing, and sputtering, favoring solvent-free processes, and even low-temperature ZnO-based TCOs still face sputter-damage issues.
evidence_spans: However, tandems have limited selection of inorganic transporting layers, because, especially for 2-T tandems, layers must be deposited using processes that are compatible with the underlying device stack.
c-Si bottom cells employing amorphous-Si passivation or TCO layers imposes upper thermal limit of < 200–250 °C

Depositing on MHP bottom cells must avoid polar solvents, high-temperature annealing, and sputtering, therefore the chosen materials should be compatible with solvent-free processes e.g., atomic layer deposition, evaporation, dry transfer139.
In tandem devices, electrode deposition must also avoid damaging the perovskite absorber or disrupting the temperature-sensitive passivation layers used in c-Si bottom cells.

These materials are generally more compatible with tandem processing because they can be deposited at lower temperatures, although sputter damage to MHP layers and amorphous Si passivation layers for c-Si remains a challenge.

constraint.content: Lead-risk mitigation is a hard design and deployment constraint: physical encapsulation alone is insufficient because catastrophic events such as hail can breach barriers, so additional Pb-sequestration or release-prevention strategies are needed; these should be scalable, low-temperature, low-solvent, and validated under realistic mechanical, environmental, and cycling conditions.
evidence_spans: But these physical barriers can be broken during deployment, for example through hail. Strategies to prevent Pb release in the event of a catastrophic failure of encapsulation are essential

future efforts should focus on developing high-capacity sequestration strategies that can readily be integrated into modules with scalable, low-temperature, low-solvent approaches, and validated under realistic mechanical, environmental, and cycling conditions

constraint.content: Operational lifetime uncertainty is a sustainability constraint because it affects economic and environmental performance and determines when substantial end-of-life module flows will arise for recycling or repurposing.
evidence_spans: the operational lifetime of MHP/Si tandems is not currently well-established, and lifetime impacts sustainability and economic metrics whilst also influencing when there will be significant end of life modules that require recycling or repurposing.

contradiction.content: The literature is divided on the environmental fate/severity of Pb released from perovskites: some studies report major increases in plant Pb uptake from soil contaminated by MHP-derived Pb, while others conclude Pb2+ is immobilized in soil.
evidence_spans: there remains debate about how severe the release of Pb would be. Whilst some studies have indicated that plants grown in soil contaminated with 250 mg kg-1 Pb2+ from MHP films exhibits orders of magnitude increases in their Pb content202, other works indicate that Pb2+ should be immobilized in soil203.

contradiction.content: There are trade-offs among design and sustainability goals across the module life cycle: stronger encapsulation to limit Pb release can hinder glass delamination and recycling; likewise, design for longevity and some manufacturing-impact reductions can worsen end-of-life recyclability, and vice versa.
evidence_spans: There are significant technical challenges, and some are contradictory. For example, improving encapsulation to prevent Pb release to the waste stream can also make delamination of glass more difficult.
design for longevity can make the module more difficult to recycle
Methods to reduce the environmental impact of producing MHP-based tandems can be both positive and negative for recycling at EOL.
